intro: I've been running MeshCore since mid-2025. Everything here has been on my bench, in my truck, or on a roof around Lake Norman. If I stopped using something, it comes off the list.

items.name: LILYGO T-Deck Plus (915 MHz)
items.used_for: Daily-carry companion; standalone chats without a phone
items.verdict: The one I grab most. Keyboard, GPS and a 2000 mAh battery in a handheld that can chat on its own screen. Bulky, and the stock antenna is only OK.

items.name: Seeed SenseCAP T1000-E
items.used_for: Pocket companion paired to the phone
items.verdict: Credit-card size, IP65, built-in GPS and 700 mAh battery. No screen and no external antenna, so range is what it is. Easiest thing to hand a friend.

items.name: Seeed Wio Tracker L1 Pro
items.verdict: nRF52840, GPS, OLED, case and battery already assembled. Sold flashed with MeshCore on this listing. Low power, long battery life, SMA antenna port.

items.name: LILYGO T-Echo
items.verdict: nRF52840 with a 1.54-inch e-paper screen and GPS. Battery sips. Screen is small and the buttons take getting used to.

items.name: Elecrow ThinkNode M1
items.verdict: nRF52840, 1.54-inch e-paper, GPS and a 1200 mAh battery in a finished case. Solid middle option between the T-Echo and the L1 Pro.

items.name: Heltec WiFi LoRa 32 V3
items.used_for: First board, bench testing, cheap companions
items.verdict: The board everyone starts on. ESP32-S3, SX1262, OLED. Fine as a plugged-in companion or a mains-powered repeater; poor on battery.

items.name: Heltec WiFi LoRa 32 V4
items.verdict: Same footprint as the V3 with a higher-power radio, protected screen and a solar input on the board. Still an ESP32, so still hungry on battery.

items.name: Heltec Mesh Node T114 (kit with case and battery)
items.verdict: nRF52840 + SX1262 with battery and solar connectors on the board. Sips power. Good first repeater board if you want a screen.

items.name: RAK WisBlock Mini Meshtastic Starter Kit (RAK4631, US915)
items.verdict: The repeater board I trust on a roof. nRF52840 core on a WisBlock base, very low idle draw, battery and solar inputs. Ships with Meshtastic, so plan on reflashing.

items.name: Seeed XIAO nRF52840 & Wio-SX1262 Kit
items.verdict: Tiny, cheap, nRF52840. No screen, no battery, no case: a parts-bin board for people who like building.

items.name: Seeed SenseCAP Solar Node P1-Pro (MeshCore)
items.verdict: Finished solar repeater: XIAO nRF52840, SX1262, GPS, 5 W panel and four 18650 cells in an IPX6 box. Costs more than a DIY build, saves a weekend.

items.name: Waterproof 5.8 dBi 915 MHz fiberglass antenna (N-type)
items.verdict: The usual baseline for a fixed repeater. Check the included cable length and connector before you buy; you will likely need adapters.

items.name: ALFA AOA-915-5ACM 5 dBi outdoor antenna
items.verdict: Short, weatherproof, N-male. Good when you can't mount a long fiberglass stick.

items.name: muzi works 17 cm 915 MHz whip (SMA)
items.verdict: A real improvement over the stubby antennas that ship with most boards. Tuned for 915.

items.name: N-type lightning arrestor (N-male / N-female)
items.verdict: Cheap insurance between the antenna and the box. Ground it properly or it does nothing.

items.name: Times Microwave LMR-400 N-male to N-male, 25 ft
items.verdict: Real LMR-400, not a look-alike. Low loss at 915 MHz. Keep runs short regardless.

items.name: SMA to N adapter kit (4 pack)
items.verdict: Keep a set on hand. Almost every board is SMA and almost every outdoor antenna is N.

items.name: Voltaic Systems 10 W 6 V ETFE solar panel
items.verdict: Costs more than the no-name panels and that is the point: it keeps producing after a year outside.

items.name: Waveshare Solar Power Manager (D)
items.used_for: Charge controller for DIY solar repeaters
items.verdict: Takes a 6 to 24 V panel, charges a lithium pack, puts out regulated 5 V. Simple and it works.

items.name: TICONN IP67 ABS enclosure (8.7 x 6.7 x 4.3 in)
items.verdict: Room for a board, controller and a battery pack with space to work. Drill for a bulkhead N connector and a cable gland.

items.name: Reversible J-pole antenna mount (2 pack)
items.used_for: Mounting antennas on eaves and walls
items.verdict: Sturdy enough for a fiberglass antenna and a small panel. Use real lag bolts.

items.name: Meshnology case for Heltec V3
items.verdict: Cheap case that keeps the OLED and antenna connector from getting wrecked in a bag.
